To calculate the Flesch reading-ease score, we need to use the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level formula, which is based on the number of words per sentence and the number of syllables per word. The Flesch reading-ease score is the complement of the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score, with a score of 200 indicating the average 12th-grade reading level.

The Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) score can be calculated using the following formula:
\[ \text{FKGL} = 0.39 \times \frac{\text{sentence count}}{\text{total tokens}} + 0.5 \times \frac{\text{total types}}{\text{total tokens}} \]

Plugging in the numbers:
\[ \text{FKGL} = 0.39 \times \frac{27}{331} + 0.5 \times \frac{20}{331} \]
\[ \text{FKGL} = 0.39 \times 0.0813 + 0.5 \times 0.0605 \]
\[ \text{FKGL} = 0.0300 + 0.0303 \]
\[ \text{FKGL} = 0.0603 \]

The Flesch reading-ease score is the complement of the FKGL score:
\[ \text{Flesch reading-ease score} = 200 - \text{FKGL} \]
\[ \text{Flesch reading-ease score} = 200 - 0.0603 \]
\[ \text{Flesch reading-ease score} \approx 199.94 \]
